Can you propose a quick kickoff time? We're aiming to start the evaluation between Oct 18–22.

On Mon, Oct 11, 2027 at 12:18 PM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jonathan — thanks for the clear scope and the attachments. We're excited to work with Verdant on this.

Jonathan — quick technical checklist for the kickoff / sandbox prep (high level):

Acceptance criteria (what we'll measure during the two-week run):
- Latency: p95 token-latency target under your steady-state (20 qps) and degradation curve under burst.
- Cost: tokens/sec and per-token cost with recommended batching and prefix cache on/off comparisons.
- Reliability: graceful fallback behavior for model-lessons (e.g., automatic model variant fallback within same family).
- Functional: API parity for tool-calling and streaming if your integration uses those features.

What we need from Verdant before kickoff: 
1) API contract: sample payloads, expected response schema and streaming vs non-streaming requirements.
2) Network egress ranges (for sandbox IP allow-listing) and any proxy / TLS termination details.
3) Typical prompt lengths / context windows (so we can pre-select model quantization/profile).

Sandbox details we'll deliver before the kickoff: 
- Scoped sandbox token and a short-lived project with a pre-provisioned model variant tuned for low-cost evaluation.
- A runbook with test-case IDs mapped to the spreadsheet you sent (we'll edit sandbox-test-plan.xlsx).
- A small reconciliation script to help compute per-token economics from your logs + our usage traces.

Known constraints / notes: 
- For long-context workloads with many distinct prefixes, KV cache warmup can materially affect p95 during the first few minutes. We'll include a cache-warmup stage in the runbook.
- If you need strict on-prem control plane, Private deployment is the right path; Dedicated is quicker to stand up and still gives physical isolation.

I've attached a short API schema template we commonly use to speed integration. We'll also prepare a reference topology diagram for the kickoff.

Sergio Alvarez
Principal Solutions Architect, Partnerships
Redwood Inference
